title: "Week 16 Self-Assessment"
subtitle: "Regression, R-Squared, and Prediction"
---



## Instructions

Test your understanding of regression analysis, the meaning of R-squared, and how we use regression for prediction. Regression builds on correlation to allow us to predict one variable from another.

---

## Part 1: Conceptual Questions

### Question 1: What is Regression?

Simple linear regression is used to:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Compare two groups</option><option value='answer'>Predict one variable from another using a linear equation</option><option value=''>Test for differences before and after</option><option value=''>Determine if variables are categorical</option></select>

In regression, the predictor variable is also called:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The dependent variable</option><option value='answer'>The independent variable (IV) or X variable</option><option value=''>The outcome</option><option value=''>The residual</option></select>

The outcome variable is also called:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The predictor</option><option value='answer'>The dependent variable (DV) or Y variable</option><option value=''>The independent variable</option><option value=''>The slope</option></select>

### Question 2: The Regression Equation

The regression equation is: Y = a + bX. In this equation:

'a' (the intercept) represents:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The slope of the line</option><option value='answer'>The predicted Y value when X = 0</option><option value=''>The correlation coefficient</option><option value=''>The sample size</option></select>

'b' (the slope) represents:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The Y-intercept</option><option value='answer'>The change in Y for each one-unit increase in X</option><option value=''>The total variance</option><option value=''>The residual</option></select>

### Question 3: Regression vs Correlation

How is regression different from correlation?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>They are exactly the same</option><option value='answer'>Regression allows prediction and has a specific direction (X predicts Y)</option><option value=''>Correlation is more accurate</option><option value=''>Regression only works with experiments</option></select>

If the correlation between X and Y is strong, the regression will:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Fail to work</option><option value='answer'>Make more accurate predictions</option><option value=''>Always predict perfectly</option><option value=''>Have a slope of zero</option></select>

### Question 4: R-Squared in Regression

R-squared (R2) tells us:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The significance level</option><option value='answer'>The proportion of variance in Y explained by X</option><option value=''>The slope of the line</option><option value=''>The sample size needed</option></select>

If R2 = .36, this means:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The correlation is .36</option><option value=''>36% of participants showed the effect</option><option value='answer'>36% of the variance in Y is explained by X</option><option value=''>The prediction is 36% accurate</option></select>

The remaining variance (1 - R2) is called:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Explained variance</option><option value='answer'>Unexplained or residual variance</option><option value=''>Total variance</option><option value=''>The intercept</option></select>

### Question 5: Residuals

A residual is:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The predicted value</option><option value=''>The slope</option><option value='answer'>The difference between the actual Y value and the predicted Y value</option><option value=''>The correlation coefficient</option></select>

If a residual is positive, the actual score was:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Lower than predicted</option><option value='answer'>Higher than predicted</option><option value=''>Exactly as predicted</option><option value=''>Cannot determine</option></select>

### Question 6: Assumptions of Regression

Linear regression assumes:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>A linear relationship between X and Y</option><option value=''>A curvilinear relationship</option><option value=''>No relationship at all</option><option value=''>Categorical variables only</option></select>

If the relationship is clearly curved (nonlinear), we should:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Use linear regression anyway</option><option value='answer'>Consider transforming variables or using nonlinear methods</option><option value=''>Ignore the pattern</option><option value=''>Collect more data</option></select>

---

## Part 2: Interpretation Questions

### Question 7: Interpreting Regression Output

A regression analysis yields: Y = 25 + 3X, R2 = .42

If X = 10, the predicted Y is:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>25</option><option value=''>30</option><option value='answer'>55</option><option value=''>42</option></select>

For every 1-unit increase in X, Y increases by:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>25</option><option value='answer'>3</option><option value=''>42</option><option value=''>10</option></select>

### Question 8: Interpreting R-Squared

Study A reports R2 = .64. Study B reports R2 = .16.

Which study's predictor explains more variance? <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Study A</option><option value=''>Study B</option><option value=''>They are equal</option><option value=''>Cannot compare</option></select>

In Study A, what percentage of variance is NOT explained?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>64%</option><option value='answer'>36%</option><option value=''>100%</option><option value=''>16%</option></select>

### Question 9: From Correlation to R-Squared

If r = .60, what is R2?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>.60</option><option value='answer'>.36</option><option value=''>6.0</option><option value=''>.30</option></select>

If r = -.50, what is R2?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>-.50</option><option value=''>-.25</option><option value='answer'>.25</option><option value=''>.50</option></select>

Note: R-squared is always positive because we square the correlation.

### Question 10: Interpreting the Slope

A regression predicting exam score from hours studied shows: Score = 50 + 5(Hours)

This means:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Everyone gets 50</option><option value='answer'>Each additional hour of study is associated with 5 more points</option><option value=''>Studying 5 hours gives a score of 50</option><option value=''>The maximum score is 55</option></select>

A student who studies 8 hours is predicted to score:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>58</option><option value=''>50</option><option value='answer'>90</option><option value=''>80</option></select>

---

## Part 3: Application Questions

### Question 11: Making Predictions

A researcher develops a regression equation to predict stress (Y) from workload (X):
Stress = 10 + 2.5(Workload), R2 = .49

For someone with a workload score of 8, predicted stress is:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>10</option><option value=''>20</option><option value='answer'>30</option><option value=''>49</option></select>

How much variance in stress is explained by workload?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>10%</option><option value=''>25%</option><option value='answer'>49%</option><option value=''>2.5%</option></select>

### Question 12: Evaluating Prediction Quality

A regression with R2 = .81 will make:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Poor predictions</option><option value='answer'>Good predictions (81% variance explained)</option><option value=''>Perfect predictions</option><option value=''>No predictions</option></select>

A regression with R2 = .09 will make:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Excellent predictions</option><option value='answer'>Poor predictions (only 9% variance explained)</option><option value=''>Moderate predictions</option><option value=''>Perfect predictions</option></select>

### Question 13: Limitations of Prediction

We should be cautious about:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Making any predictions</option><option value='answer'>Predicting beyond the range of observed data (extrapolation)</option><option value=''>Using regression at all</option><option value=''>Large R-squared values</option></select>

If our data has X values ranging from 1-10, predicting Y when X = 50 is:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Very reliable</option><option value='answer'>Unreliable extrapolation</option><option value=''>More accurate than interpolation</option><option value=''>Impossible</option></select>

---

## Part 4: MCQ Exam Practice

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 1

A researcher examines whether hours of practice predicts piano performance scores. Data from 40 students yields: Performance = 30 + 4(Practice Hours), R2 = .52, p < .001.

1. **What type of analysis is this?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>t-test</option><option value=''>Correlation only</option><option value='answer'>Simple linear regression</option><option value=''>ANOVA</option></select>

2. **Predictor (IV):** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Practice hours</option><option value=''>Performance score</option><option value=''>Sample size</option><option value=''>R-squared</option></select>

3. **Outcome (DV):** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Practice hours</option><option value='answer'>Performance score</option><option value=''>The slope</option><option value=''>The intercept</option></select>

4. **For each additional hour of practice, performance increases by:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>30 points</option><option value='answer'>4 points</option><option value=''>52 points</option><option value=''>1 point</option></select>

5. **A student who practices 10 hours is predicted to score:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>30</option><option value=''>40</option><option value='answer'>70</option><option value=''>100</option></select>

6. **How much variance in performance is explained?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>30%</option><option value=''>4%</option><option value='answer'>52%</option><option value=''>70%</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 2

A study finds that sleep quality (X) predicts daily mood (Y) with R2 = .25.

1. **What percentage of variance in mood is explained by sleep quality?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>75%</option><option value='answer'>25%</option><option value=''>50%</option><option value=''>5%</option></select>

2. **What is the correlation (r) between sleep and mood?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>.25</option><option value='answer'>.50 (since R2 = .25, r = sqrt(.25) = .50)</option><option value=''>.75</option><option value=''>.125</option></select>

3. **What percentage of variance is NOT explained?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>25%</option><option value='answer'>75%</option><option value=''>50%</option><option value=''>100%</option></select>

4. **This unexplained variance could be due to:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Other factors affecting mood (exercise, social contact, stress, etc.)</option><option value=''>Errors in R-squared</option><option value=''>The sample being too large</option><option value=''>Sleep quality being irrelevant</option></select>

5. **Can we say sleep quality CAUSES better mood?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 3

A regression equation is: Test Score = 40 + 0.5(Study Minutes), R2 = .36

1. **The intercept (40) represents:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Predicted score when study time = 0</option><option value=''>The slope</option><option value=''>R-squared</option><option value=''>The maximum score</option></select>

2. **Studying for 60 minutes predicts a score of:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>40</option><option value=''>60</option><option value='answer'>70</option><option value=''>100</option></select>

3. **Studying for 120 minutes predicts a score of:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>60</option><option value=''>80</option><option value='answer'>100</option><option value=''>120</option></select>

4. **A student actually scored 80 after studying 60 minutes. Their residual is:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>-10</option><option value='answer'>+10 (actual 80 minus predicted 70)</option><option value=''>0</option><option value=''>80</option></select>

5. **The positive residual means they scored:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Higher than predicted</option><option value=''>Lower than predicted</option><option value=''>Exactly as predicted</option><option value=''>We cannot tell</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 4

A researcher wants to predict job satisfaction from salary. R2 = .15.

1. **How would you evaluate this R2?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Excellent - salary fully explains satisfaction</option><option value='answer'>Modest - salary explains only 15% of variance in satisfaction</option><option value=''>R2 is too small to interpret</option><option value=''>Perfect prediction</option></select>

2. **What does this suggest about other factors?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>No other factors matter</option><option value='answer'>85% of variance is due to other factors (work environment, colleagues, autonomy, etc.)</option><option value=''>Salary is the only factor</option><option value=''>We cannot speculate</option></select>

3. **Should we conclude salary doesn't matter for satisfaction?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>No - it still explains some variance; other factors also matter</option><option value=''>Yes - 15% is too small</option><option value=''>The study is invalid</option><option value=''>We need a larger sample</option></select>

4. **Multiple regression could help by:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Removing the effect of salary</option><option value='answer'>Including additional predictors to explain more variance</option><option value=''>Making R2 exactly 1.0</option><option value=''>Eliminating residuals</option></select>

:::

---

## Summary Checklist

Before moving on, make sure you can:

- [ ] Explain the purpose of regression analysis
- [ ] Interpret the regression equation (Y = a + bX)
- [ ] Understand what the intercept (a) and slope (b) represent
- [ ] Calculate predicted values using a regression equation
- [ ] Interpret R-squared as proportion of variance explained
- [ ] Convert between r and R-squared
- [ ] Explain what residuals represent
- [ ] Recognise limitations of prediction (extrapolation)

::: {.callout-important}
## Key Distinction
Correlation tells us about the strength and direction of a relationship. Regression goes further by providing a specific equation for prediction and quantifying how much variance is explained. However, regression (like correlation) still cannot establish causation without an experimental design.
:::
